correctness.rationale: The exact second variation along the in-phase invariant manifold gives the audited scalar normal equation. Substitution of the reported apparatus parameters independently reproduces the release stiffness at 47.8 degrees and the static sign-loss angle near 84.43 degrees, so the observed onset cannot be a release-point stiffness sign change. The quadratic expansion of the in-phase trajectory gives the listed combination channels and a nonzero sum-frequency coefficient. The repository verifier was read from its guarded Git blob and its recorded numerical values agree with the independent calculation; the finite computation is used only to check arithmetic, not as a proof of the variational equation.

originality.rationale: The motivating Toda–Ooshida work studies measured energy transfer into the antiphase mode and discusses the near relation between the two in-phase frequencies and twice the antiphase frequency. Its accessible full-paper rendering emphasizes that the observed threshold is not a universal static critical angle and does not present the audited exact normal variational equation or the 84.43-degree release-stiffness boundary. Resultary found no earlier record implying this exact finite-amplitude transverse equation and local quadratic forcing statement.

value.rationale: The exact normal equation separates a genuine transverse dynamical instability mechanism from a tempting but incorrect static release-stiffness explanation and gives a reusable Hill-equation starting point for Floquet analysis of the experiment. The frequency-channel calculation then identifies a mathematically motivated local forcing mechanism without overclaiming the finite-amplitude threshold.
